clue.text: Free from follicle fillings on top, like a fulika

definitions.text: Free from follicle fillings on top, like a fulika

parts.words: Free from follicle fillings on top, like a fulika
parts.note: a roundabout way of saying hairless on the crown, as a certain water bird with a white forehead patch seems to be; Fulica is that bird's scientific genus

explanation.surface: A mock-scientific description of a bare scalp compared to a water bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair fills follicles, so a head free of follicle fillings on top is hairless; the coot's white frontal shield makes it look bald, hence the simile, and Fulica is the coot's Latin genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for completely hairless, from the bare-looking white patch on the bird's head.

clue.text: The thing a doctor carries on his round

indicators.note: carries on means continues, so the thing comes on after a doctor

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
it is the pronoun for the thing

explanation.surface: A general practitioner taking something along on visits to patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries on' looks like the doctor carrying a bag on visits, but it means 'continues with', placing the thing last; 'round' in the sense of scope or compass is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the bounds or circuit of something, its compass or sphere.

clue.text: A seed is mutated by blight

indicators.note: mutated means changed in form, so the letters of A SEED IS are changed in order

explanation.surface: A plant seed changing for the worse because of a fungal infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutated' rearranges A SEED IS; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight is a plant disorder, so the two words are synonyms for an affliction.

clue.text: Train a shoal of fish

definitions.meaning: to train is to educate or drill someone
a group of fish swimming together has this name too

explanation.surface: A command to teach a group of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to educate; the other is the collective noun for fish, as with whales and porpoises.

clue.text: Armour also used as underwear

definitions.meaning: a woman's foundation garment combining corset and bra

explanation.surface: A garment that served as protection in battle and also as lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a piece of body armour and a light corset, two different garments for the torso.

clue.text: Two-bore gun more than adequate for this attempt?

definitions.text: Two-bore gun more than adequate for this attempt?

parts.words: Two-bore gun more than adequate for this attempt?
parts.note: a double-barrelled gun fires twice, which is more than you need when you only get a single go

explanation.surface: A hunter with a double-barrelled gun finding it excessive for the task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-bore' suggests a gun's gauge, but here it means two barrels, each giving a shot, which is more than a single try requires.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a single attempt, a go that will not be repeated.

clue.text: To arm Africa, we bring about nuclear conflict

indicators.note: bring about can mean turn round, as a ship is brought about, so the preceding letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that militarising a continent will trigger an atomic war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring about' reads as cause, but it signals that TO ARM AFRICA WE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic weapons are nuclear weapons, so war fought with them is nuclear conflict.

clue.text: Seating place that's been avoided by married lady?

definitions.text: Seating place that's been avoided by married lady?

parts.words: Seating place that's been avoided by married lady?
parts.note: a woman who did wed escaped being left on the ledge where unmarried women were said to sit

explanation.surface: Somewhere a wife has never had to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on the shelf' is the old idiom for being unmarried and past the age of likely marriage, so a married lady has avoided it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ledge is the place spinsters were idiomatically said to be left sitting.

clue.text: The first clues are very influential

definitions.text: The first clues are very influential

parts.words: The first clues are very influential
parts.note: in crosswords the answers are called lights, so the opening ones lead; the phrase also means prominent people

explanation.surface: A claim that the opening hints in a puzzle matter most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' is crossword jargon for answers in the grid, so the first ones are 'leading'; the whole phrase also means eminent, influential people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for prominent figures who influence others.

clue.text: Piping for the bath at two points

parts.note: a tub is a bath
E and S are east and south, two points of the compass

explanation.surface: Pipework needed to plumb a bath at two places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' are compass points, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of pipe are a set of hollow cylinders, so piping in the plural sense.

clue.text: Lucky Arab's mule?

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of steed, and a mule can be a backless slipper, so this is a steed's lucky footwear

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fortunate Middle Eastern man's pack animal is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' looks like a person and 'mule' like an animal, but an Arab is a horse breed and a mule is a slipper, so this is the horse's footwear, a good-luck charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron fitted to a hoof is a traditional token of good fortune.

clue.text: Subterranean dwelling said to be of greater significance

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: to matter more is to be of greater significance

explanation.surface: Something spoken about being more important.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattamore is an underground chamber, a cellar or pit used as a dwelling or store.

clue.text: At hospital, nasty dose is swilled down with water

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: nasty suggests the word dose is spoilt, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital washes down an unpleasant medicine with water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' signals the rearrangement of the word dose, which follows the hospital letter; 'is' links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose something is to wash it with a jet of water.

clue.text: If worn, is seriously restrictive?

parts.note: a tight necklace worn close to the throat, which taken literally would throttle its wearer

explanation.surface: A warning about tight clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a garment that constricts; the joke is the name of the close-fitting necklace, which literally means something that strangles.
explanation.definitionFit: The necklace fits tightly round the throat, and its name means a thing that strangles.

clue.text: Underwent reverse, but prevailed

parts.note: take the opposite of each part of underwent: under becomes over and went becomes came, giving a word meaning won

explanation.surface: Someone suffered a setback but won in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like a setback, but it tells you to swap each part of 'underwent' for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win through, to beat an obstacle.

clue.text: Find out about the hide

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for find out goes round the next word

parts.note: to learn is to find out

explanation.surface: Discover what is going on concerning the animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'hide' stands for the adjective 'of hide', made of tanned skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern means made of tanned skin, an old adjective for leather goods.

clue.text: Give the gang weapons and means of identification

definitions.meaning: to supply a group with arms
bands worn on the upper arm to show who someone is or what role they hold

explanation.surface: Arming a gang and handing out identity badges.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means arm gangs; as one it names sleeve bands worn to identify officials.

clue.text: Hole reached by scrambling right up a tree

indicators.note: scrambling means mixing up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A hollow found by clambering up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambling' suggests climbing, but it means mixing up R plus UP A TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening or gap.

clue.text: Crumbling to dust, first ever Roman air-raid shelter?

indicators.note: crumbling means breaking up, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
first picks out the opening letter of ever

explanation.surface: Something reduced to dust, the first-ever bomb shelter in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: TO DUST plus E is rearranged; the Roman 'tortoise' was soldiers locking shields overhead against arrows and stones from above, humorously an air-raid shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise formation of interlocked shields protected Roman troops from missiles falling from above.

clue.text: Handy arrangement of flues beyond the bend

indicators.note: beyond means after, so the rearranged letters come after the bend

parts.note: a U-bend is the curved pipe, shaped like U

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Plumbing advice: chimney pipes placed past the bend work well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' signals a reordering of the word flues, which goes after the letter shaped like a U-bend in plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy means of practical use, convenient.

clue.text: Colonist who pays his bills?

definitions.meaning: one who goes to live in a new land
one who settles an account pays it

explanation.surface: A pioneer who is also good with money.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a pioneer in a new land; the other is one who settles debts.

clue.text: Old hunter needing game to shoot

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matches from piles
rod is gangster slang for a gun, something to shoot with

explanation.surface: An ancient hunter wanting quarry to fire at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests quarry, but it is the matchstick game NIM; Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible calls Nimrod a mighty hunter, so his name stands for any huntsman.

clue.text: Fine book providing hard information

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A good book that supplies solid data.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts are hard data, verified information.

clue.text: Seeing red sprat biting end of bait?

indicators.note: biting means taking into the mouth, so the fish holds the letter

parts.note: a brisling is a sprat, a small fish

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of bait

explanation.surface: A small fish taking the bait at the end of a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing red' looks like a description but is the definition: angrily bristling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristling means showing anger, like an animal's hair standing up.

clue.text: Being trendy, acquired a bar

parts.note: in means fashionable
got means acquired

explanation.surface: Becoming fashionable and buying a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal such as gold.

clue.text: The odd athlete a smuggler?

parts.note: rum means strange or odd
a runner is an athlete

explanation.surface: An eccentric runner turns out to be a smuggler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is British for odd; a rumrunner smuggled liquor, especially during Prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumrunner smuggled liquor across borders.

clue.text: You'll be converted if you see it!

definitions.text: You'll be converted if you see it!

parts.words: You'll be converted if you see it!
parts.note: an idiom for being converted or realising the truth

explanation.surface: A preacher's promise of conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: To see the light is an idiom for religious conversion or sudden understanding.

clue.text: Thoughtful judge had a meal

parts.note: to consider is to judge or weigh up
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A kind magistrate who dined.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerate means kind and attentive to others.
